reapack.desc: CuePort Sync — Artist comments as markers

metadata.description: {\rtf1\ansi\deflang1033 {\fonttbl{\f0\fswiss\fcharset0 Helvetica;}} \f0\fs22 \fs28\b CuePort Sync\b0\fs22\par \par Reaper integration for CuePort. The comments on a production, the artist's and the studio's, threads and all, are pulled into your project as native markers and drawn on a waveform inside the window. You can answer them from the DAW, delete a reply again, switch between every version the studio has uploaded, and send a new render back as a version without leaving Reaper.\par \par \b Features\b0\par - Device-code pairing with the CuePort studio portal, no passwords in the script\par - Production picker grouped by artist, with cover art and an inline search\par - Waveform of the active version with the comments pinned on it, click or drag to move the DAW cursor\par - Comment list beside it or below the production: the whole thread, artist and studio, replies indented\par - Amber for the artist, violet for the studio, blue for a label, cyan for a guest, on the pins and the timestamps\par - The production's own tracks, in the studio's order and under their names\par - Reply to a comment from the DAW, and delete a reply you sent\par - Project markers for the comments, optional, and a marker where the open version begins\par - Every version remembers where it begins in the project, and the ruler's 0:00 follows it\par - A/B compare against the uploaded version, routed past the master so the finished bounce stays uncolored\par - Render straight from Reaper and send it back as a new version, without the browser\par - The render settings are borrowed for the one pass and put back byte for byte afterwards\par - The finished render is shown to you first, with its length, its waveform and anything that looks off\par - Light and dark like the studio portal, or following Reaper's theme, in the portal's nine brand colors\par - Survives a dropped connection: requests are retried, an upload pauses and carries on\par - Reaper's shortcuts keep working after a click in the window (needs JS_ReaScriptAPI, space bar without)\par - Floating transport pill for one-click sync while the window is out of the way\par - Keeps itself up to date, through ReaPack when it manages this copy\par - Per-project binding, so every .rpp remembers its own production and version\par \par \b Requirements\b0\par - Reaper 6.68 or later\par - \b ReaImGui\b0 (install via ReaPack, required)\par - \b curl\b0 (bundled with Windows 10 and later, macOS and Linux)\par - \b SWS Extension\b0 (recommended, for reliable hover detection)\par - \b JS_ReaScriptAPI\b0 (recommended)\par \par \b Setup\b0\par 1. Install this package via ReaPack.\par 2. Open the Reaper Actions list and run \b cueport_sync.lua\b0 .\par 3. Open CuePort in your browser, generate a pairing code, and type it into the plugin.\par 4. Pick a production and bind it to the open .rpp.\par 5. Click \b Sync comments\b0 . Done.\par \par \b Time alignment\b0\par Every version remembers where it begins in your project, stored in CuePort. A render sent from the script brings it along; for a version uploaded in the browser, set it once from the edit cursor. The ruler's 0:00 follows the open version, so CuePort's comment times are your ruler's times; turn that off in Settings and your own Project start time comes back.\par \par MIT licensed. The full text, the third-party notices and a list of everything the script touches in your project are on the About screen in the script itself.\par }

version.changelog:
CuePort Sync 1.39.1
Only one version is listed here, and it is the one that is really on the server. Older builds are not kept, so listing them would offer downloads that cannot be delivered.
FIXED IN 1.39.1
In light mode the menu opened as a dark panel. It now follows the theme.
WHAT CHANGED IN 1.39.0
1. Light, dark or auto, in the studio's colors. - New in Settings, Appearance: Light, Dark or Auto. Auto follows the brightness of your Reaper theme. - Pick one of the nine brand colors of the CuePort studio portal (CuePort, Blue, Teal, Green, Orange, Red, Pink, Gold, Graphite). The whole window follows it: buttons, switches and the background gradient. - Dark with CuePort looks exactly as before.
2. Comments are colored by who wrote them, as in the portals. Amber for the artist, violet for the studio, cyan for a guest, blue for a label, on the pins and on the timestamps.
3. The production's own tracks. If the studio set up its own tracks for a production, the script shows exactly those, in the studio's order and under their names. A track that is planned but has no version yet stays visible and dimmed. Uploading a render suggests the track that is open in the player, otherwise the production's delivery track. With an older server the script shows Instrumental and Mix Master as before.
4. Reaper's shortcuts keep working after a click in the window. Until now a click into the script kept the keyboard, and Reaper's shortcuts did nothing until you clicked back into Reaper. Now the keyboard goes back to Reaper right after a click, unless you are typing into a field. Needs JS_ReaScriptAPI; without it only the space bar (play and stop) is passed on. Switch in Settings, Window: Shortcuts go to Reaper, on by default.
5. A dropped connection no longer stops the script. After a longer pause, a laptop waking up or a network change, the first request could fail with "the host could not be resolved". Requests that never reached the server are now retried a few times. An upload pauses instead of giving up, keeps the parts already sent and carries on with Try again. The error message says in plain words what went wrong.
6. Smaller things. - A reply you may not delete (a label's reply, unless you are an admin) no longer shows the delete cross. - A failed delete or reply shows its full reason under the COMMENTS heading instead of a cut-off line. - A broken cover image shows the placeholder instead of stopping the script. - The comment list below the production fills the docker down to its end. - Narrow dockers wrap labels instead of cutting them off. - The background gradient is smooth instead of banded. - The file name of an upload never contains characters Windows, macOS or Linux reject.
Earlier releases: see the repository history.
